Rule set evolution (R(t)) is modeled as a stochastic process driven by strategic necessity and lack of precedent. Institutional adoption (A(I,t)) reflects a contagion-like mechanism where early adopters like Harvard influence others such as Yale. Strategic innovation (S) arises from the game’s structure enabling complex tactics and individual brilliance. These three operators form a triadic system: R(t) evolves through A(I,t), while S is both a driver and consequence of R(t). The failure mode occurs when R(t) becomes too rigid or when A(I,t) fails to propagate effectively. Dualities emerge in how institutional behavior mirrors strategic complexity—both are emergent properties of shared rule structures. The breakdown regime occurs when strategic novelty cannot be encoded into rules or when institutions resist change. This framework allows for modeling the evolution of complex systems through rule-based interaction and institutional learning.
